title: Support selecting comparison systems
body:
## Summary

- Add `compare --systems` to select writer systems, allowing baseline and candidate comparisons without a native writer; preserve the selection when resuming and rebuilding experiments.
- Show cross-model composite score deltas and bootstrap intervals in accuracy reports.

title: Add compare system selection and composite score deltas
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
`compare` previously ran all three provider systems and judged the candidate against both baseline and native. The new `--systems` option can omit native while retaining the baseline and candidate writers; in that case only candidate versus baseline is judged, in both orders. It accepts short and full system names, defaults to all three, and requires baseline and candidate.

Planning, execution, rebuilt coverage and the quality gate follow the selected systems. Subsets are frozen in the manifest and experiment identity; all-three runs retain the prior identity, and a resume without `--systems` uses the frozen selection.

The accuracy view also adds a composite-score delta to its cross-model candidate-versus-baseline table, with a 95% bootstrap interval over shared cases using per-case means.

Start review with system selection in `src/run/provider.ts` and its use in `src/comparison.ts`; the comparison and score tests exercise the subset and composite contrast.

title: Select comparison systems and report composite deltas
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Comparing graph quality and cost across models calls for a smaller test matrix and a composite score comparison. This change lets a comparison omit the native writer and reports the composite delta across candidate and baseline model arms.

Previously, comparisons planned and rebuilt judgments against both the baseline and the provider's native system. `compare --systems` now accepts `native`, `baseline`, and `candidate`, their full names, or the provider's native name; it defaults to all three and requires baseline and candidate. Writers follow the selected systems; when native is omitted, candidate is judged against baseline in both orders. Planned counts, rebuild coverage, and quality gates reflect the selection, and plan output includes `systems` and `judgedAgainst`. A subset is stored in manifest settings and experiment identity, while all three retain the previous identity; resuming without `--systems` uses the frozen selection.

For candidate and baseline arms with shared cases, the accuracy table now includes candidate-minus-baseline composite delta and a 95% bootstrap interval over per-case means. `tests/comparison.test.ts` covers frozen three-system runs, matching-artifact resumes, and planning and resuming without native; `tests/score.test.ts` checks the case-clustered interval. The comparison tests use a fake setup rather than the real comparison setup.

## Validation
